verdict: OK to lend in Faridabad tractors and farm machinery — back dealer and component borrowers with verifiable festive-season cash flow, avoid pure retail tractor financiers and inventory-heavy dealers until the price hike settles.
title: Faridabad tractors & farm machinery: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
A Faridabad tractor borrower is usually one of three things: a dealer/distributor moving OEM units into Haryana and NCR mandis, a component or implement maker feeding the Faridabad–Farrukhnagar belt, or a retail financier carrying the farmer's EMI. **Cash turns on the festive and rabi sowing calendar, not on the calendar year.** The dealer buys from the OEM on credit, holds yard inventory, sells against part-cash and part-finance, and collects the finance leg through a tie-up NBFC. So when a proposal lands, check the dealer's OEM credit terms and the share of sales routed through tied-up financiers; if the financier leg is above half of sales, ask for the financier's settlement record.

## Where value and cash sit
**Value sits in the OEM franchise and the service/parts annuity, not in the metal.** Peers show the margin story: Escorts Kubota's Q4 revenue rose 21.4% to Rs 29.51 billion with profit up 9.2% to Rs 3.25 billion [5][6], and M&M holds 44% tractor market share at Q3FY26 with core tractor margins near peak [4]. That tells you the OEMs have pricing room; the dealer does not. Working capital is the risk: yard stock plus receivables from financiers.

## What has changed now
**Escorts Kubota is raising tractor prices across Kubota, Farmtrac and Powertrac after the festive season, citing input costs [2][3].** A price hike mid-season squeezes dealers holding pre-hike stock and can stall retail conversion. Note the local tailwind: Haryana GST collections grew 10.1% Apr-to-date against India's 6.1% [D], and India-wide IIP for NIC 28 is +10.3% YoY [D]. But the rating view is cautious — CRISIL saw tractors declining 2-4% on high base, weaker rabi profitability and elevated inventory [9], and that report is old, so treat it as direction, not forecast. Escorts sold 16,921 units in October 2026 [1]; collect from customer the Faridabad-specific split of that.

Structure dealer limits as cash-credit against stock and receivables with a 25% margin, and component makers on term loan plus working capital with DSRA of one quarter. Take every month: stock statement, financier-wise receivables, OEM dispatch invoices, and GST returns. Covenant a debt-service coverage floor and a stock-turn floor; if stock turn falls below the sanctioned norm for two months, freeze the drawing power.

- **GST turnover diverging from bank credits** — check monthly; if the gap widens two months running, call for the sales register. - **OEM price-hike pass-through failing at retail** — track dealer realisation monthly; if realisation falls while invoice cost rises, reprice the limit.
watch: Monthly GST returns vs bank credits
Turnover-credit gap widening two months running -> call for sales register and re-assess limit
Quarterly OEM dispatch and price circulars
Price hike not passed to retail realisation -> reprice limit and raise margin
Coverage below covenant floor -> restructure tenure or seek promoter infusion
